title: csm-orchestrate approach fidelity and residual limitations: pass 2 challenge

tldr.content: Pass 2 verdict: pass 1 was directionally correct but under-specified the trust model. The implementation remains a contract-safe prototype. To address the residual limitations, the host must enforce authenticated delegation, independent review attestation, exact request-bound approvals, linearizable ownership/history, durable cancellation reconciliation, and evidence-derived evaluation gates.

executiveSummary.content:
Four independent challengers re-tested pass 1 against the repository and current authority sources. They upheld the core fidelity assessment, downgraded optimism around signatures and local review, and added concrete gaps: missing activation-predicate execution, missing required external-input rejection, cross-process duplicate dispatch, timeout-side-effect ambiguity, incomplete compatibility integration, and receipt semantic inconsistency. The recommended solution is now an assurance protocol around the existing controller, not a claim that the controller alone can create trust.

pass 1 finding -> independent challenges -> corrected invariants -> production-blocking conditions

keyFindings.content:
K1. upheld: Canonical phases, capability metadata, typed handoffs, bounded local scheduling, and status projection are implemented, but runtime-object immutability is not durable immutability [R1][R2].
K2. upheld: Structural signal IDs are not semantic entailment; critical signals require an independent reproducible validator over the exact artifact digest [R3][R4].
K3. downgraded: Host-backed review is a fail-closed controller boundary, not proof that the host isolated or honestly executed the reviewer [R3][R5].
K4. not-supported: Cross-process durable coordination, exactly-once side effects, and cancellation completion are not supplied by the current interfaces [R6][R7].
K5. upheld: Pass 1’s remediation direction preserves the architecture, but must add activation predicates, budget consumption, physical insertion, complete request approvals, and compatibility negotiation [R1][R3].
K6. supported: Production rollout requires instrumentation, a held-out corpus, independent blinded adjudication, shadow/canary comparison, and tested rollback; current tests are not outcome evidence [R8][R9].

detailSections.content:
Correction to the trust model: a signature authenticates an attestation but does not prove reviewer correctness. The relying party must verify signer authorization, audience, freshness, nonce/replay status, subject digest, review policy digest, and exact input set. The same distinction applies to artifact resolver output and approvals: controller fields are assertions unless anchored by the host, issuer, or trusted artifact index.

Correction to the durability model: the process-local WeakMap queue serializes writes only within one process. It cannot prevent two coordinators from both observing an absent cursor and dispatching the same child. Required primitives are compare-and-set, fencing tokens, durable idempotency indexes, atomic dispatch intent, monotonic terminal state, and a history that can reconstruct every request and late result. A timeout must be treated as unknown until the side-effect boundary reconciles it.

Correction to the evidence model: an acceptanceSignalId is a routing key, not a proof. Each critical signal must have an executable or independently reproducible predicate, validator identity/version, exact resolved artifact digest, immutable input snapshot, result, and review policy digest.

Correction to rollout: use replay/shadow mode first, then an isolated canary against a contemporaneous control. Measure terminal availability, false VERIFIED, false rejection, duplicate effects, recovery, p95/p99 latency, retry amplification, cost, correction rate, reviewer agreement, and telemetry completeness. Stop rules must be stricter for safety failures than for benign incompleteness.

recommendation.content: Keep csm-orchestrate fail-closed and do not enable production autonomy yet. Address the limitations in this order: (1) specify the authenticated host/delegation and artifact-index protocol; (2) implement exact request-digest approvals and durable CAS/fencing/history; (3) make signal validators and reviewer attestations independent and reproducible; (4) execute remediation budgets and insertion ordering; (5) instrument traces/metrics; (6) validate on held-out workloads with blinded adjudication; (7) run a bounded shadow/canary only after rollback and telemetry-loss behavior are tested. A durable workflow engine or transactional outbox may be used beneath the controller, but neither removes the need for external-effect reconciliation.

unverifiedClaims.content: The real host’s signer trust, reviewer process isolation, approval issuer, artifact-index authority, CAS/fencing semantics, cancellation acknowledgement, late side-effect reconciliation, workload representativeness, sample size, human agreement, cost model, and canary isolation are unknown. The exact compatible schema migration semantics also require end-to-end version-negotiation tests rather than helper-only tests.

references.content: Pass 2 rechecked local claims against commit d2fd905 and current authority sources retrieved 2026-08-27. References include SLSA verification, RATS, OAuth authorization, JSON Schema, Temporal/Cloudflare durable execution, etcd transactions, OpenTelemetry, Google SRE, and NIST AI RMF.

processAppendix.content: Pass 2 consumed pass 1 and dispatched four independent read-only challenge tracks: fidelity, security/provenance, durability/recovery, and operability/evaluation. The challengers did not edit the repository. They upheld, downgraded, or added claims and supplied corrected invariants and validation experiments. Pass 3 will adversarially review both saved findings and produce the final report.

claims.statement: The structural controller mechanisms are largely implemented, but object freezing and schema validation do not by themselves create durable immutable history or semantic correctness.
Matching requirement and acceptance-signal IDs remain insufficient to prove that an artifact satisfies the signal; independent appraisal is required.

The host review path is fail-closed against unmarked callbacks, but the controller cannot prove that a host-issued reviewer was isolated, authorized, fresh, or semantically correct without an authenticated attestation protocol.
The current process-local cursor queue and in-memory idempotency state do not prevent cross-process duplicate dispatch or establish exactly-once external side effects.

Remediation budget consumption, physical insertion ordering, required external-input rejection, and activation-predicate execution are concrete fidelity requirements rather than optional host features.
Production rollout should be deferred until trace/metric instrumentation, held-out evaluation, independent blinded adjudication, and tested rollback/telemetry-loss stop rules exist.
